title: Finite presentation relative to R survives localization: M of finite presentation over R_f becomes M_g of finite presentation over R
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma concerns a finite type ring map R_f -> A, an element g of A and an A-module M of finite presentation relative to R_f, and asserts that M_g is of finite presentation relative to R, not merely relative to R_f (statement lines 21014-21020). The proof is neither a citation nor a formal manipulation: it rewrites the localization R_f as R[x_0]/(f x_0 - 1), lifts the presentation of A, of the element g and of every matrix entry to the polynomial ring over R, and then exhibits an explicit t by (s + 2t) matrix whose three blocks encode the original relations together with the two localization relations f x_0 - 1 and x_{n+1} g' - 1 (proof lines 21023-21044). The point of the construction is precisely the change of base from R_f to R, so that the same module is seen to be finitely presented over R itself. The counted span is self-contained: it refers to no labelled item of the chapter and cites nothing; the printed text writes M_f where the construction presents M_g, and that slip is preserved verbatim.
